4. **Addressing Key Research Challenges**

This section outlines how the key challenges identified in predicting forex prices such as volatility, integration of economic indicators, sentiment analysis, noise in data, and overfitting were addressed in the research.

* **High Volatility:** Forex markets are known for their high volatility, which complicates accurate predictions. To address this, the research uses LSTM and Transformer models, which excel in capturing long-term dependencies and patterns in sequential data. Addi- tionally, the models are trained on both short-term (four-hour) and long-term (one-day) time frames, ensuring that they can adapt to varying market conditions.

* **Economic Indicators Integration:** The integration of various economic indicators into predictive models can be complex due to the diverse nature of the data. In this research, XGBoost is used to handle structured data, such as economic indicators, by efficiently managing non-linear relationships between multiple features. By combining technical and fundamental data, the model captures both short-term and long-term factors influ- encing forex prices.

* **Sentiment Analysis Integration:** Sentiment analysis provides valuable insights into market sentiment but poses challenges in integrating unstructured data with traditional technical and fundamental indicators. This research employs LLMs such as GPT-4 and GEMINI Advanced for sentiment extraction from financial news. These sentiment scores are then incorporated into the prediction models, allowing the model to consider market sentiment alongside traditional indicators.

* **Noise in Data:** Financial data is often noisy, which can obscure meaningful patterns and lead to inaccurate predictions. To reduce the impact of noise, this research employs pre- processing techniques such as feature selection and data smoothing. Ensemble methods, such as the combination of XGBoost and LSTM, also help mitigate the effects of noisy data by leveraging multiple models for more robust predictions.

* **Overfitting:** Overfitting is a common issue in financial forecasting, where models per- form well on training data but fail to generalize to unseen data. In this study, overfitting is mitigated through the use of regularization techniques, cross-validation, dropout and early stopping during model training. These techniques ensure that the model generalizes well to new data.

By addressing these challenges systematically, the research develops more robust and accurate forex prediction models, capable of adapting to the volatile and complex nature of the forex market.

4. **Results and Analysis**

This section presents the results and analysis of the predictive models, focusing on their perfor- mance across different configurations and forex pairs. Specifically, the analysis covers models that utilise only technical indicators, models based on fundamental indicators, models integrat- ing both technical and fundamental indicators, and models that incorporate sentiment analysis alongside technical and fundamental indicators. For each pair, the predictive accuracy of the models is assessed using a comprehensive suite of evaluation metrics. This section aims to determine the most effective combination of indicators and model configurations for accurate forex price prediction, providing insights into each approach’s practical applicability and ro- bustness.

1. **Technical Models (TM)**

The performance of the technical models (TM) on test data using the OHLC one-day time- frame is summarised in Table [2\.](#table-2:-model-performance-on-test-data-using-technical-indicators-with-ohlc-one-day-time-frame) This table highlights the results for various models, includ- ing LSTM TM, XGBoost TM, Ensemble-LSTM-XGB TM, TRANSFORMER EN DE TM,

and TRANSFORMER DE TM, evaluated across four currency pairs: EUR/USD, NZD/USD, EUR/NZD, and AUD/NZD.

The LSTM TM model shows strong performance across all currency pairs, particularly with AUD/NZD, which achieved an RMSE of 0.0037. The XGBoost TM model demonstrated exceptional accuracy, especially for EUR/NZD and AUD/NZD, with RMSE values of 0.0048 and 0.0017, respectively, indicating a very high level of precision. The Ensemble-LSTM- XGB TM model combines the strengths of both LSTM and XGBoost, resulting in improved performance metrics for EUR/USD and NZD/USD, achieving RMSE values of 0.0064 and 0.0039, respectively.

The Transformer-based models, both the encoder-decoder (TRANSFORMER EN DE TM) and the decoder-only (TRANSFORMER DE TM) architectures, showed varied performance.

While they did not outperform the LSTM or XGBoost models overall, they still provided valuable insights, particularly for EUR/NZD and AUD/NZD, with the encoder-decoder model achieving an RMSE of 0.0148 for EUR/NZD and the decoder-only model achieving an RMSE of 0.0051 for AUD/NZD.

This section evaluates models combining technical and fundamental indicators (TM FM) over a one-day timeframe. The LSTM TM FM model performs well, especially for EUR/NZD, with an MAE of 0.0476 and an RMSE of 0.0123. For EUR/USD, this model achieves an MAE of 0.1140, a MAPE of 1.2640%, and an RMSE of 0.0159. The Ensemble model, which combines LSTM and XGBoost (Ensemble-LSTM-XGB TM FM), best performs for EUR/USD and NZD/USD pairs. Using a weighted average of predictions from both models, an MAE of 0.0092 and an RMSE of 0.0118 for EUR/USD are achieved. For NZD/USD, it records an MAE of 0.0037 and an RMSE of 0.0052, highlight- ing the advantage of integrating multiple model architectures to improve predictive accuracy. Transformer models, TRANSFORMER EN DE TM FM, and TRANSFORMER DE TM FM architectures perform less effectively than LSTM and XGBoost models. The TRANSFORMER EN DE TM FM model has an RMSE of 0.0306 for EUR/USD and 0.0184 for NZD/USD, in- dicating that while Transformer models can capture complex dependencies in sequential data, they are not as effective in this context as LSTM and XGBoost models.

4. **Technical, Fundamental, and Sentiment Models (TM FM SA)**

This section presents the performance evaluation of models that integrate technical indicators, fundamental indicators, and sentiment analysis (TM FM SA) in a Four-hour timeframe. Table [5](#table-5:-model-performance-on-test-data-with-technical,-fundamental,-and-sentiment-analysis-on-a-4h-timeframe) summarises the results of these models across the four forex pairs. The LSTM TM FM SA model shows varying performance across currency pairs. For EUR/USD, it achieves an MAE of 0.0906, a MAPE of 0.1364%, and an RMSE of 0.0020, with an R² of 0.8967. The model per- forms similarly well for EUR/NZD with an MAE of 0.0811 and an RMSE of 0.0043. However, the model’s performance on NZD/USD and AUD/NZD pairs is comparatively lower, indicating that while LSTM can effectively integrate multiple data types, its accuracy can vary depending on the currency pair.

The XGBoost TM FM SA model significantly outperforms other models in this inte- grated approach, particularly for EUR/USD and NZD/USD pairs. For EUR/USD, the model achieves a remarkably low MAE of 0.0007, a MAPE of 0.0707%, and an RMSE of 0.0010, with an R² of 0.9897. The performance is similarly vital for NZD/USD, EUR/NZD, and AUD/NZD, indicating that XGBoost excels in leveraging technical, fundamental, and sentiment data to en- hance predictive accuracy. The Ensemble-LSTM-XGB TM FM SA model also shows robust performance, particularly for EUR/USD and NZD/USD pairs. The ensemble approach, which uses weighted averaging to combine the predictions of both models, achieves a good balance between the strengths of LSTM and XGBoost. For EUR/USD, it achieves an MAE of 0.0008, a MAPE of 0.0759%, and an RMSE of 0.0010, with an R² of 0.9873.

The Transformer models, both TRANSFORMER EN DE TM FM SA and TRANS- FORMER DE TM FM SA architectures, exhibit lower performance compared to LSTM and XGBoost models. For instance, the TRANSFORMER EN DE TM FM SA model achieves an RMSE of 0.0042 for EUR/USD, significantly higher than the XGBoost model. This suggests that while Transformer models are powerful in capturing complex dependencies in sequential data, their performance in this context is less effective than LSTM and XGBoost.

Table [5](#table-5:-model-performance-on-test-data-with-technical,-fundamental,-and-sentiment-analysis-on-a-4h-timeframe) clearly shows that integrating technical indicators, fundamental indicators, and sentiment analysis data enhances the predictive capabilities of the models, with XGBoost lead- ing in accuracy and the ensemble model providing a balanced performance across different currency pairs. This comprehensive integration approach effectively captures the multifaceted nature of forex market movements, offering valuable insights for forex price prediction.

5. **Analysis and Discussion**

In the previous section, the performance results of various predictive models were presented, highlighting their effectiveness in forecasting forex prices based on technical, fundamental, and combined indicators. This section is a detailed analysis of these results. This analysis will help to identify the most effective approaches for forex price prediction and provide insights into how these models can be further improved for better generalisation and practical application in

real-world scenarios.

Figure 29: Comparative Analysis of RMSE Values Across Forex Currency Pairs Using Different Pre- diction Models for One Day Time Frame.

Figure [29](#figure-29:-comparative-analysis-of-rmse-values-across-forex-currency-pairs-using-different-pre--diction-models-for-one-day-time-frame.) reveals that models using technical indicators alone consistently achieved the lowest RMSE values across all currency pairs when compared to models using fundamental indicators and those combining both types of indicators.

For the EUR/USD pair, the technical model attained an RMSE of 0.0064, which is significantly lower than the RMSE values for the fundamental model (0.0155) and the com- bined model (0.0118). Similarly, the technical model for NZD/USD had an RMSE of 0.0039, outperforming both the fundamental model (0.0057) and the combined model (0.0052). The EUR/NZD pair followed the same pattern, with the technical model achieving the lowest RMSE of 0.0048, compared to 0.0068 for the fundamental model and 0.0061 for the combined model. The AUD/NZD pair also demonstrated the superior performance of the technical model, with an RMSE of 0.0017, lower than both the fundamental model (0.0029) and the combined model (0.0025).

These results indicate that technical indicators alone provide the most accurate forecasts for forex prices in these scenarios. The technical indicators are derived directly from the OHLC data, which might explain their superior performance. The inclusion of fundamental indicators did not significantly improve the predictive accuracy and, in some cases, slightly increased

the RMSE. However, while the technical models show the lowest RMSE, the combined use of technical and fundamental indicators could still be valuable. Combining both approaches might help generalise the model better, potentially offering robustness against different market conditions and reducing overfitting. Therefore, while technical indicators appear to be the most effective for minimising RMSE in this study, the integration of both technical and fundamental indicators may provide a more generalised and potentially more resilient forecasting model in the long run.

Next, the discussion will focus on analysing the Four-hour time frame data, integrating technical, fundamental, and sentiment indicators to assess the performance of different models. By examining the correlation between sentiment scores and the ROC 9 indicator and evaluating the predictive accuracy through various metrics, the aim is to determine the most effective model configurations for short-term forex market forecasting.

Figure 30: ROC 9 Spearman Correlation of Sentiment Analysis on Forex Pairs Using Four-Hour Time Frame Data

Figure [30](#figure-30:-roc-9-spearman-correlation-of-sentiment-analysis-on-forex-pairs-using-four-hour-time-frame-data) shows the Spearman correlation coefficients between sentiment scores and the ROC 9 indicator for the EUR/USD, NZD/USD, EUR/NZD, and AUD/NZD currency pairs. The GPT-4 model demonstrated a higher correlation for EUR/USD (0.260) and NZD/USD (0.210) than the GEMINI Advanced model. Conversely, GEMINI Advanced showed a stronger correlation for EUR/NZD (0.190), while both models performed similarly for AUD/NZD. These results guided the selection of sentiment analysis models, with GPT-4 chosen for EUR/USD and NZD/USD and GEMINI Advanced for EUR/NZD, enhancing the predictive accuracy of our models.

A key observation from the results is the consistently superior performance of the XG- Boost models, particularly noted for their lower RMSE values across most currency pairs. This

exceptional performance is detailed in Table [5:](#table-5:-model-performance-on-test-data-with-technical,-fundamental,-and-sentiment-analysis-on-a-4h-timeframe)

* The XGBoost model combined with technical, fundamental, and sentiment analysis (XG- Boost TM FM SA) achieved the lowest RMSE of 0.001022 for the EUR/USD pair, in- dicating high predictive accuracy, as visually represented in Figure [25\.](#figure-25:-performance-of-the-xgboost-tm-fm-sa-model-on-eur/usd-test-data.)

* Similarly, for the NZD/USD and EUR/NZD pairs, the same XGBoost configuration re- ported RMSE values of 0.000924 and 0.002145, respectively, outperforming other model setups.

* For the AUD/NZD pair, the XGBoost TM FM SA model also demonstrated superior performance with the lowest RMSE of 0.000594, further confirming its robustness across different forex markets, as shown in Figure [28\.](#figure-28:-performance-of-the-xgboost-tm-fm-sa-model-on-aud/nzd-test-data.)

These results underscore the effectiveness of XGBoost in handling complex datasets where multiple data streams are integrated. The analysis also reveals varying levels of perfor- mance across different models and currency pairs, illustrating the complexity of forex market forecasting. The R2 values complement the RMSE results by providing insights into the vari- ance the models explain, with higher R2 indicating better model fit to the data.

Figure 31: Performance of the XGB TM model on EUR/USD Test Data.

The use of ensemble models in forex price prediction highlights the significant improve- ment in performance and generalisation of test data. As illustrated in Figure [31](#figure-31:-performance-of-the-xgb-tm-model-on-eur/usd-test-data.) and Figure [32,](#figure-32:-performance-of-the-lstm-tm-model-on-eur/usd-test-data.) both XGBoost and LSTM models individually demonstrate robust predictive capabilities. The XGBoost model excels in handling complex datasets and capturing non-linear relationships,

while the LSTM model effectively leverages its sequential memory structure to model tempo- ral dependencies.

Figure 32: Performance of the LSTM TM model on EUR/USD Test Data.

However, the ensemble model, which combines the strengths of both XGBoost and LSTM, further enhances predictive accuracy and generalisation, as shown in Figure [13\.](#figure-13:-performance-of-the-ensemble-lstm-xgb-tm-model-on-eur/usd-test-data.) By integrating these models through a weighted average technique, the ensemble model mitigates the individual weaknesses of each model, leading to more accurate and reliable predictions. This approach harnesses the superior generalisation capability of ensemble learning, reducing overfitting and improving performance across various market conditions.

1. **Addressing the Research Questions**

**Research Question 1: How do technical indicators compare with models, including fun- damental indicators and sentiment analysis, in predicting forex prices?**  
As demonstrated in Figure [29,](#figure-29:-comparative-analysis-of-rmse-values-across-forex-currency-pairs-using-different-pre--diction-models-for-one-day-time-frame.) models using technical indicators alone consistently out- performed those incorporating both fundamental and sentiment indicators, particularly for the one-day time frame. For example, the technical model for EUR/USD achieved the lowest RMSE, indicating the effectiveness of technical models in capturing immediate market move- ments. Although combined models integrating fundamental and sentiment indicators offer broader market insights, their inclusion did not lead to lower RMSE values, suggesting that technical indicators are better suited for short-term forex price predictions.

**Research Question 2: How does sentiment analysis affect the accuracy of forex price predictions?**

The analysis in Figure [30](#figure-30:-roc-9-spearman-correlation-of-sentiment-analysis-on-forex-pairs-using-four-hour-time-frame-data) demonstrates how sentiment analysis improves prediction ac- curacy, particularly for the four-hour time frame. The positive correlation between sentiment scores and the ROC 9 indicator, especially for EUR/USD and NZD/USD pairs, suggests that sentiment analysis significantly enhances short-term model performance. The results indicate that sentiment analysis plays an important role in improving the accuracy of forex price predic- tions when combined with technical indicators.

**Research Question 3: Which machine learning or deep learning models most effectively integrate these different data types for forex prediction?**  
The findings, as shown in Table [5,](#table-5:-model-performance-on-test-data-with-technical,-fundamental,-and-sentiment-analysis-on-a-4h-timeframe) highlight the superior performance of XGBoost and Ensemble-LSTM-XGB models in integrating technical, fundamental, and sentiment data. XGBoost consistently delivered the lowest RMSE values across most currency pairs, demon- strating its ability to handle complex datasets with multiple data sources. Additionally, the Ensemble-LSTM-XGB model enhanced accuracy by leveraging the strengths of both LSTM and XGBoost, making it a robust approach for integrating diverse data types in forex predic- tion.

5. **Conclusion**

This research effectively demonstrated the improvement of forex prediction accuracy by inte- grating sentiment analysis derived from LLMs with technical and fundamental data analyses. By employing LLMs such as GPT-4 and GEMINI Advanced, this study could leverage unla- belled financial news data to generate sentiment scores combined with traditional forex market data. Using Spearman correlation coefficients to assess the alignment between sentiment scores and the Rate of Change (ROC 9\) indicators was pivotal. This analysis helped determine the most effective LLM for each currency pair based on how closely sentiment changes mirrored market movements. For instance, the selected LLMs exhibited varying degrees of correlation with the ROC 9, guiding the choice of sentiment analysis model for integration into the forex prediction framework, as shown in Figure [30\.](#figure-30:-roc-9-spearman-correlation-of-sentiment-analysis-on-forex-pairs-using-four-hour-time-frame-data)

The findings, as evidenced in Tables [2,](#table-2:-model-performance-on-test-data-using-technical-indicators-with-ohlc-one-day-time-frame) [3,](#table-3:-model-performance-on-test-data-using-fundamental-indicators-with-ohlc-one-day-time-frame) [4,](#table-4:-model-performance-on-test-data-using-technical-and-fundamental-indicators-with-ohlc-one-day-time-frame) and [5,](#table-5:-model-performance-on-test-data-with-technical,-fundamental,-and-sentiment-analysis-on-a-4h-timeframe) indicate that the decoder-only ar- chitecture of Transformers exhibits promising results in forex prediction, outperforming the encoder-decoder framework. Moreover, our comparative analysis, as depicted in Figure [29,](#figure-29:-comparative-analysis-of-rmse-values-across-forex-currency-pairs-using-different-pre--diction-models-for-one-day-time-frame.) has demonstrated that technical models outperform those based on fundamental indicators or a combination of both. This could be attributed to the direct reflection of market sentiments and patterns captured in technical data, which these models distill and interpret.

The Ensemble-LSTM-XGB model combined with technical indicators achieved the best RMSE values for most currency pairs for the one-hour data analysis. Specifically, the best-performing models and their RMSE values are as follows: For the EUR/USD pair, the Ensemble-LSTM-XGB with technical indicators had an RMSE of 0.0064, while the Trans- former with an encoder-decoder architecture was the worst, with an RMSE of 0.0259, as seen in Table [2\.](#table-2:-model-performance-on-test-data-using-technical-indicators-with-ohlc-one-day-time-frame) For the NZD/USD pair, the Ensemble-LSTM-XGB with technical indicators had an RMSE of 0.0039, and the Transformer with an encoder-decoder architecture performed the worst with an RMSE of 0.0176. The EUR/NZD pair showed the XGBoost with techni- cal indicators as the best performer with an RMSE of 0.0048, while the Transformer with an encoder-decoder architecture had the highest RMSE of 0.0148. For the AUD/NZD pair, the XGBoost with technical indicators was the best, with an RMSE of 0.0017, and the Transformer with an encoder-decoder architecture was the worst, with an RMSE of 0.0051, as detailed in Table [2\.](#table-2:-model-performance-on-test-data-using-technical-indicators-with-ohlc-one-day-time-frame)

For the four-hour data analysis, the XGBoost model combined with technical, funda- mental, and sentiment indicators showed the lowest RMSE values across various currency pairs. For the EUR/USD pair, the XGBoost with technical, fundamental, and sentiment analysis had an RMSE of 0.0010, while the LSTM with technical, fundamental, and sentiment analysis had the highest RMSE of 0.0020, as shown in Table [5\.](#table-5:-model-performance-on-test-data-with-technical,-fundamental,-and-sentiment-analysis-on-a-4h-timeframe) For the NZD/USD pair, the XGBoost with technical, fundamental, and sentiment analysis had an RMSE of 0.0009, with the LSTM model performing the worst with an RMSE of 0.0042. The EUR/NZD pair performed best with the XGBoost model with an RMSE of 0.0021 and worst with the LSTM model with an RMSE

of 0.0043. For the AUD/NZD pair, the XGBoost with technical, fundamental, and sentiment analysis had the lowest RMSE of 0.0005, while the LSTM model had the highest RMSE of 0.0017.

Most compelling is the revelation from Figure [11](#figure-11:-architecture-of-the-ensemble-model-combining-lstm-and-xgboost.) that employing ensemble methods, integrating the strengths of XGBoost and LSTM models through a weighted average tech- nique, significantly improves model robustness and generalisability. Such ensemble models have shown superior performance in our study, underpinning their potential as a robust frame- work for future forex market analysis. The use of ensemble models in forex price prediction highlights the significant improvement in performance and generalisation of test data. As illus- trated in Figure [31](#figure-31:-performance-of-the-xgb-tm-model-on-eur/usd-test-data.) and Figure [32,](#figure-32:-performance-of-the-lstm-tm-model-on-eur/usd-test-data.) both XGBoost and LSTM models individually demonstrate robust predictive capabilities. The XGBoost model excels in handling complex datasets and capturing non-linear relationships, while the LSTM model effectively leverages its sequential memory structure to model temporal dependencies.

However, the ensemble model, which combines the strengths of both XGBoost and LSTM, further enhances predictive accuracy and generalisation, as shown in Figure [13\.](#figure-13:-performance-of-the-ensemble-lstm-xgb-tm-model-on-eur/usd-test-data.) By integrating these models through a weighted average technique, the ensemble model mitigates the individual weaknesses of each model, leading to more accurate and reliable predictions. This approach harnesses the superior generalisation capability of ensemble learning, reducing overfitting and improving performance across various market conditions.

**Research and Practical Implications**

The results of this study have important implications for both academic research and fi- nancial practice. The significant improvement in forex prediction accuracy, particularly through the use of ensemble methods, adds to the growing body of evidence supporting the integration of machine learning and deep learning models in financial forecasting. For researchers, this study presents a robust framework for further exploration of hybrid and ensemble approaches in financial time-series prediction, highlighting the potential for advanced models like LSTM and XGBoost to work in concert for enhanced accuracy.

In practice, the integration of sentiment analysis with technical and fundamental indica- tors offers traders and financial institutions a more comprehensive toolkit for predicting forex market movements. The demonstrated effectiveness of combining these data sources can help practitioners develop more reliable models that better capture market complexities, enabling them to make more informed trading decisions. Additionally, the demonstrated robustness of ensemble models suggests their use in developing automated trading algorithms that can adapt to diverse market conditions and reduce the risks associated with overfitting.

**Future Research Directions**

While this study produced promising results, several avenues for future research re- main. One area of interest is the inclusion of real-time data processing to assess how these models perform under dynamic market conditions. Furthermore, exploring more advanced sentiment analysis techniques such as those derived from social media or geopolitical analysis

could further enhance prediction accuracy. Future studies could also delve into the potential of combining more sophisticated ensemble techniques, such as stacking or blending, to improve performance.

Expanding the range of economic and geopolitical factors considered in the models would offer additional insights into forex price movements, potentially leading to even more precise predictions. This research lays the groundwork for future advancements in the field of financial forecasting, pushing the boundaries of machine learning and deep learning applica- tions in trading and decision-making.

Nonlinear nexus between cryptocurrency returns and COVID-19 news sentiment

a b s t r a c t

The paper examines how various COVID-19 news sentiments differentially impact the behaviour of cryptocurrency returns. We used a nonlinear technique of transfer entropy to investigate the relationship between the top 30 cryptocurrencies by market capitalisation and COVID-19 news sentiment. Results show that COVID-19 news sentiment influences cryptocurrency returns. The nexus is unidirectional from news sentiment to cryptocurrency returns, in contrast to past findings. These results have practical implications for policymakers and market participants in understanding cryptocurrency market dynamics under extremely stressful market conditions.

1. **Introduction**

Signalling theory documents the importance of news as sig- nals to perceive future market behaviour ([Connelly et al.](#conlon,-t.,-corbet,-s.,-mcgee,-r.j.,-2020.-are-cryptocurrencies-a-safe-haven-for-equity-markets?-an-international-perspective-from-the-covid–19-pandemic.-res.-int.-bus.-finance-54,-101248.), [2011](#conlon,-t.,-corbet,-s.,-mcgee,-r.j.,-2020.-are-cryptocurrencies-a-safe-haven-for-equity-markets?-an-international-perspective-from-the-covid–19-pandemic.-res.-int.-bus.-finance-54,-101248.)). The framework asserts the role of the signaller and the signal, and whenever the signal contains new or vital information, the markets tend to react accordingly to new signals ([Fu et al.](#frijns,-b.,-huynh,-t.d.,-2018.-herding-in-analysts’-recommendations:-the-role-of-media.-j.-bank.-financ.-91,-1–18.), [2021](#frijns,-b.,-huynh,-t.d.,-2018.-herding-in-analysts’-recommendations:-the-role-of-media.-j.-bank.-financ.-91,-1–18.); [Romer](#rognone,-l.,-hyde,-s.,-zhang,-s.s.,-2020.-news-sentiment-in-the-cryptocurrency-market:-an-empirical-comparison-with-forex.-int.-rev.-financ.-anal.-69,-101462.), [1993](#rognone,-l.,-hyde,-s.,-zhang,-s.s.,-2020.-news-sentiment-in-the-cryptocurrency-market:-an-empirical-comparison-with-forex.-int.-rev.-financ.-anal.-69,-101462.); [Wei and Zhou](#wang,-p.,-zhang,-w.,-li,-x.,-shen,-d.,-2019.-is-cryptocurrency-a-hedge-or-a-safe-haven-for-international-indices?-a-comprehensive-and-dynamic-perspective.-finance-res.-lett.-31,-1–18.), [2016](#wang,-p.,-zhang,-w.,-li,-x.,-shen,-d.,-2019.-is-cryptocurrency-a-hedge-or-a-safe-haven-for-international-indices?-a-comprehensive-and-dynamic-perspective.-finance-res.-lett.-31,-1–18.)). Numerous news signals are available in the public domain and are used to understand as- set pricing behaviour ([Gan et al.](#195–205.), [2020](#195–205.); [Sanford](#salisu,-a.a.,-ogbonna,-a.e.,-2021.-the-return-volatility-of-cryptocurrencies-during-the-covid–19-pandemic:-assessing-the-news-effect.-glob.-financ.-j.-100641.), [2020](#salisu,-a.a.,-ogbonna,-a.e.,-2021.-the-return-volatility-of-cryptocurrencies-during-the-covid–19-pandemic:-assessing-the-news-effect.-glob.-financ.-j.-100641.)). Extant literature has supported that whenever news is unavailable in the public domain and it is released with a degree of surprise, the vibrancy in the markets is equally visible in prices and trad- [ing](#banerjee,-a.k.,-padhan,-p.c.,-2017.-herding-behavior-in-futures-market:-an-empirical-analysis-from-india.-ssrn-3014561.) volume ([García et al.](#garcia,-d.,-2013.-sentiment-during-recessions.-j.-finance-68-\(3\),-1267–1300.), [2014](#garcia,-d.,-2013.-sentiment-during-recessions.-j.-finance-68-\(3\),-1267–1300.); [Banerjee et al.](#banerjee,-a.k.,-pradhan,-h.k.,-2021b.-did-precious-metals-serve-as-hedge-and-safe--haven-alternatives-to-equity-during-the-covid-19-pandemic:-new-insights-using-a-copula-based-approach.-ssrn-3934171.), [2020](#banerjee,-a.k.,-pradhan,-h.k.,-2021b.-did-precious-metals-serve-as-hedge-and-safe--haven-alternatives-to-equity-during-the-covid-19-pandemic:-new-insights-using-a-copula-based-approach.-ssrn-3934171.); [Banerjee](#banerjee,-a.k.,-padhan,-p.c.,-2017.-herding-behavior-in-futures-market:-an-empirical-analysis-from-india.-ssrn-3014561.) [and Pradhan](#banerjee,-a.k.,-padhan,-p.c.,-2017.-herding-behavior-in-futures-market:-an-empirical-analysis-from-india.-ssrn-3014561.), [2020a](#banerjee,-a.k.,-padhan,-p.c.,-2017.-herding-behavior-in-futures-market:-an-empirical-analysis-from-india.-ssrn-3014561.), [2021a](#banerjee,-a.k.,-pradhan,-h.k.,-2020b.-order-flows,-investor-sentiments-and-feedback-trade-in-index-futures-market.-j.-quant.-econ.-18-\(4\),-767–782.)). The impact of such news on various asset classes such as bonds, cur- [rencies,](#banerjee,-a.k.,-dionisio,-a.,-pradhan,-h.k.,-mahapatra,-b.,-2021.-hunting-the-quicksilver:-using-textual-news-and-causality-analysis-to-predict-market-volatility.-int.-rev.-financ.-anal.-77,-101848.) stocks and futures markets is well-documented ([Banerjee](#banerjee,-a.k.,-dionisio,-a.,-pradhan,-h.k.,-mahapatra,-b.,-2021.-hunting-the-quicksilver:-using-textual-news-and-causality-analysis-to-predict-market-volatility.-int.-rev.-financ.-anal.-77,-101848.) [Miwa](#marsh,-i.w.,-wagner,-w.,-2016.-news-specific-price-discovery-in-credit-default-swap-markets.-financ.-manage.-45-\(2\),-315–340.), [2019](#marsh,-i.w.,-wagner,-w.,-2016.-news-specific-price-discovery-in-credit-default-swap-markets.-financ.-manage.-45-\(2\),-315–340.); Recently studying the credit default markets (CDS), [Marsh](#marsh,-i.w.,-wagner,-w.,-2016.-news-specific-price-discovery-in-credit-default-swap-markets.-financ.-manage.-45-\(2\),-315–340.) [and Wagner](#marsh,-i.w.,-wagner,-w.,-2016.-news-specific-price-discovery-in-credit-default-swap-markets.-financ.-manage.-45-\(2\),-315–340.) ([2016](#marsh,-i.w.,-wagner,-w.,-2016.-news-specific-price-discovery-in-credit-default-swap-markets.-financ.-manage.-45-\(2\),-315–340.)) have asserted that swap dealers exploit the informational advantages against investors. [Wei and Zhou](#wang,-p.,-zhang,-w.,-li,-x.,-shen,-d.,-2019.-is-cryptocurrency-a-hedge-or-a-safe-haven-for-international-indices?-a-comprehensive-and-dynamic-perspective.-finance-res.-lett.-31,-1–18.) ([2016](#wang,-p.,-zhang,-w.,-li,-x.,-shen,-d.,-2019.-is-cryptocurrency-a-hedge-or-a-safe-haven-for-international-indices?-a-comprehensive-and-dynamic-perspective.-finance-res.-lett.-31,-1–18.)) documented the surge in bond trading activity before the re- lease of earning announcements in the expectation of information asymmetry in news signals. [Bailey et al.](#baek,-s.k.,-jung,-w.s.,-kwon,-o.,-moon,-h.t.,-2005.-transfer-entropy-analysis-of-the-stock-market.-arxiv-preprint-physics/0509014.) ([2014](#baek,-s.k.,-jung,-w.s.,-kwon,-o.,-moon,-h.t.,-2005.-transfer-entropy-analysis-of-the-stock-market.-arxiv-preprint-physics/0509014.)) reported a signifi- cant association between changes in the volatility index (VIX) and macroeconomic announcements by studying the high-frequency changes in VIX. Past literature has found a causal impact on financial journalism, media news and aggregate market prices ([Banerjee et al.](#banerjee,-a.k.,-2021.-futures-market-and-the-contagion-effect-of-covid–19-syndrome.-finance-res.-lett.-102018.), [2021](#banerjee,-a.k.,-2021.-futures-market-and-the-contagion-effect-of-covid–19-syndrome.-finance-res.-lett.-102018.); [Dougal et al.](#ding,-z.,-granger,-c.w.,-engle,-r.f.,-1993.-a-long-memory-property-of-stock-market-returns-and-a-new-model.-j.-empir.-financ.-1-\(1\),-83–106.), [2012](#ding,-z.,-granger,-c.w.,-engle,-r.f.,-1993.-a-long-memory-property-of-stock-market-returns-and-a-new-model.-j.-empir.-financ.-1-\(1\),-83–106.)) and how management

disclosures work as a signal that drives investors ([Koonce et al.](#kim,-s.,-ku,-s.,-chang,-w.,-song,-j.w.,-2020.-predicting-the-direction-of-us-stock-prices-using-effective-transfer-entropy-and-machine-learning-techniques.-ieee-access-8,-111660–111682.), [2016](#kim,-s.,-ku,-s.,-chang,-w.,-song,-j.w.,-2020.-predicting-the-direction-of-us-stock-prices-using-effective-transfer-entropy-and-machine-learning-techniques.-ieee-access-8,-111660–111682.)). Some varied examples of signalling theory are initial public offering (IPO) pricing, news sentiments influencing stock returns at the aggregate market level ([Cutler et al.](#corbet,-s.,-lucey,-b.,-urquhart,-a.,-yarovaya,-l.,-2019.-cryptocurrencies-as-a-financial-asset:-a-systematic-analysis.-int.-rev.-financ.-anal.-62,-182–199.), [1989](#corbet,-s.,-lucey,-b.,-urquhart,-a.,-yarovaya,-l.,-2019.-cryptocurrencies-as-a-financial-asset:-a-systematic-analysis.-int.-rev.-financ.-anal.-62,-182–199.); [Garcia](#gan,-b.,-alexeev,-v.,-bird,-r.,-yeung,-d.,-2020.-sensitivity-to-sentiment:-news-vs-social-media.-int.-rev.-financ.-anal.-67,-101390.), [2013](#gan,-b.,-alexeev,-v.,-bird,-r.,-yeung,-d.,-2020.-sensitivity-to-sentiment:-news-vs-social-media.-int.-rev.-financ.-anal.-67,-101390.); [Tetlock](#subramaniam,-s.,-chakraborty,-m.,-2020.-investor-attention-and-cryptocurrency-returns:-evidence-from-quantile-causality-approach.-j.-behav.-finance-21-\(1\),-103–115.), [2007](#subramaniam,-s.,-chakraborty,-m.,-2020.-investor-attention-and-cryptocurrency-returns:-evidence-from-quantile-causality-approach.-j.-behav.-finance-21-\(1\),-103–115.)) and the individual stock level ([Boudoukh et al.](#boudoukh,-j.,-feldman,-r.,-kogan,-s.,-richardson,-m.,-2013.-which-news-moves-stock-prices?-a-textual-analysis-\(no.-w18725\).-national-bureau-of-economic-research.), [2013](#boudoukh,-j.,-feldman,-r.,-kogan,-s.,-richardson,-m.,-2013.-which-news-moves-stock-prices?-a-textual-analysis-\(no.-w18725\).-national-bureau-of-economic-research.); [Chen et al.](#cheah,-e.t.,-fry,-j.,-2015.-speculative-bubbles-in-bitcoin-markets?-an-empirical-investigation-into-the-fundamental-value-of-bitcoin.-econom.-lett.-130,-32–36.-chen,-h.,-de,-p.,-hu,-y.j.,-hwang,-b.-h.,-2014.-wisdom-of-crowds:-the-value-of-stock-opinions-transmitted-through-social-media.-rev.-financ.-stud.-27-\(5\),), [2014](#cheah,-e.t.,-fry,-j.,-2015.-speculative-bubbles-in-bitcoin-markets?-an-empirical-investigation-into-the-fundamental-value-of-bitcoin.-econom.-lett.-130,-32–36.-chen,-h.,-de,-p.,-hu,-y.j.,-hwang,-b.-h.,-2014.-wisdom-of-crowds:-the-value-of-stock-opinions-transmitted-through-social-media.-rev.-financ.-stud.-27-\(5\),)). Information uncertainty originating from news sentiment increases expected stock return, thus affecting stock returns negatively ([Zhang](#youssef,-m.,-2020.-what-drives-herding-behavior-in-the-cryptocurrency-market?-j.-behav.-finance-1–10.), [2006](#youssef,-m.,-2020.-what-drives-herding-behavior-in-the-cryptocurrency-market?-j.-behav.-finance-1–10.)). Thus, the above reinstates that information asymmetry remains the mainstay of signalling theory, with the information intent and quality the critical factors ([Stiglitz](#stavroglou,-s.k.,-pantelous,-a.a.,-stanley,-h.e.,-zuev,-k.m.,-2019.-hid--den-interactions-in-financial-markets.-proc.-natl.-acad.-sci.-116-\(22\),-10646–10651.), [2002](#stavroglou,-s.k.,-pantelous,-a.a.,-stanley,-h.e.,-zuev,-k.m.,-2019.-hid--den-interactions-in-financial-markets.-proc.-natl.-acad.-sci.-116-\(22\),-10646–10651.)).  
Currently, the literature has begun exploring the impact of news on newer asset classes such as cryptocurrencies, which are drawing much attention for their diversification properties and hedging role. Moreover, the assumption that analysing the impact of news on cryptocurrency returns may reveal newer perspec- tives is gaining ground in the literature ([Bouri and Gupta](#bouri,-e.,-gkillas,-k.,-gupta,-r.,-2020.-trade-uncertainties-and-the-hedging-abilities-of-bitcoin.-econ.-notes-49-\(3\),-e12173.), [2019](#bouri,-e.,-gkillas,-k.,-gupta,-r.,-2020.-trade-uncertainties-and-the-hedging-abilities-of-bitcoin.-econ.-notes-49-\(3\),-e12173.); [Bouri](#1112–1130.) [et al.](#bouri,-e.,-gabauer,-d.,-gupta,-r.,-tiwari,-a.k.,-2021a.-volatility-connectedness-of-major-cryptocurrencies:-the-role-of-investor-happiness.-j.-behav.-exp.-financ.-30,-100463.), [2020](#bouri,-e.,-gabauer,-d.,-gupta,-r.,-tiwari,-a.k.,-2021a.-volatility-connectedness-of-major-cryptocurrencies:-the-role-of-investor-happiness.-j.-behav.-exp.-financ.-30,-100463.); [Naeem et al.](#moldovan,-a.,-caţaron,-a.,-andonie,-r.,-2020.-learning-in-feedforward-neural-networks-accelerated-by-transfer-entropy.-entropy-22-\(1\),-102.-http://dx.doi.-org/10.3390/e22010102.), [2021](#moldovan,-a.,-caţaron,-a.,-andonie,-r.,-2020.-learning-in-feedforward-neural-networks-accelerated-by-transfer-entropy.-entropy-22-\(1\),-102.-http://dx.doi.-org/10.3390/e22010102.); [Rognone et al.](#raimundo-júnior,-g.d.s.,-palazzi,-r.b.,-tavares,-r.d.s.,-klotzle,-m.c.,-2020.-market-stress-and-herding:-a-new-approach-to-the-cryptocurrency-market.-j.-behav.-finance-1–15.), [2020](#raimundo-júnior,-g.d.s.,-palazzi,-r.b.,-tavares,-r.d.s.,-klotzle,-m.c.,-2020.-market-stress-and-herding:-a-new-approach-to-the-cryptocurrency-market.-j.-behav.-finance-1–15.); [Sal-](#1112–1130.) [isu and Ogbonna](#1112–1130.), [2021](#1112–1130.)). Over the past decade, cryptocurrencies have seen remarkable growth and received extensive attention from market players interested in determining the driving fac- tors behind price formation ([Aharon](#agbloyor,-e.k.,-abor,-j.,-adjasi,-c.k.d.,-yawson,-a.,-2013.-exploring-the-causality-links-between-financial-markets-and-foreign-direct-investment-in-africa.-res.-int.-bus.-finance-28,-118–134.), [2020](#agbloyor,-e.k.,-abor,-j.,-adjasi,-c.k.d.,-yawson,-a.,-2013.-exploring-the-causality-links-between-financial-markets-and-foreign-direct-investment-in-africa.-res.-int.-bus.-finance-28,-118–134.); [Ciaian et al.](#1367–1403.), [2016](#1367–1403.); [Kristoufek](#amer.-econ.-rev.-92-\(3\),-460–501.), [2013](#koonce,-l.,-seybert,-n.,-smith,-j.,-2016.-management-speaks,-investors-listen:-are-investors-too-focused-on-managerial-disclosures?-j.-behav.-finance-17-\(1\),-31–44.); [Raimundo Júnior et al.](#poyser,-o.,-2019.-exploring-the-dynamics-of-bitcoin’s-price:-a-bayesian-structural-time-series-approach.-eurasian-econ.-rev.-9-\(1\),-29–60.), [2020](#poyser,-o.,-2019.-exploring-the-dynamics-of-bitcoin’s-price:-a-bayesian-structural-time-series-approach.-eurasian-econ.-rev.-9-\(1\),-29–60.); [Subramaniam](#amer.-econ.-rev.-92-\(3\),-460–501.) [and Chakraborty](#amer.-econ.-rev.-92-\(3\),-460–501.), [2020](#amer.-econ.-rev.-92-\(3\),-460–501.); [Youssef](#wei,-j.,-zhou,-x.,-2016.-informed-trading-in-corporate-bonds-prior-to-earnings-announcements.-financ.-manage.-45-\(3\),-641–674.), [2020](#wei,-j.,-zhou,-x.,-2016.-informed-trading-in-corporate-bonds-prior-to-earnings-announcements.-financ.-manage.-45-\(3\),-641–674.)). However, cryptocurren- cies have a unique price, volume, and risk features ([Sifat](#shi,-y.,-ho,-k.y.,-2021.-news-sentiment-and-states-of-stock-return-volatility:-evidence-from-long-memory-and-discrete-choice-models.-finance-res.-lett.-38,-101446.), [2021](#shi,-y.,-ho,-k.y.,-2021.-news-sentiment-and-states-of-stock-return-volatility:-evidence-from-long-memory-and-discrete-choice-models.-finance-res.-lett.-38,-101446.)). Due to this uniqueness, cryptocurrency valuation is challenging ([Ciaian et al.](#1367–1403.), [2016](#1367–1403.)). In addition, the literature on the mecha- nism of how news and sentiment influence cryptocurrency return is evolving ([Corbet et al.](#corbet,-s.,-larkin,-c.,-lucey,-b.m.,-meegan,-a.,-yarovaya,-l.,-2020a.-the-impact-of-macroeconomic-news-on-bitcoin-returns.-eur.-j.-finance-26-\(14\),-1396–1416.), [2019](#corbet,-s.,-larkin,-c.,-lucey,-b.m.,-meegan,-a.,-yarovaya,-l.,-2020a.-the-impact-of-macroeconomic-news-on-bitcoin-returns.-eur.-j.-finance-26-\(14\),-1396–1416.); [Naeem et al.](#naeem,-m.a.,-mbarki,-i.,-shahzad,-s.j.h.,-2021.-predictive-role-of-online-investor-sentiment-for-cryptocurrency-market:-evidence-from-happiness-and-fears.-int.-rev.-econ.-finance-73,-496–514.), [2020](#naeem,-m.a.,-mbarki,-i.,-shahzad,-s.j.h.,-2021.-predictive-role-of-online-investor-sentiment-for-cryptocurrency-market:-evidence-from-happiness-and-fears.-int.-rev.-econ.-finance-73,-496–514.); [Poyser](#porfiri,-m.,-2018.-inferring-causal-relationships-in-zebrafish-robot-interactions-through-transfer-entropy:-a-small-lure-to-catch-a-big-fish.-animal-behav.-cogn.-5-\(4\),-341–367.), [2019](#porfiri,-m.,-2018.-inferring-causal-relationships-in-zebrafish-robot-interactions-through-transfer-entropy:-a-small-lure-to-catch-a-big-fish.-animal-behav.-cogn.-5-\(4\),-341–367.)). The present paper contributes to the debate on how news and sentiment affect cryptocurrency prices, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic.  
Apart from examining the effect of news sentiment on cryp- tocurrency return, we attempt to determine whether the nexus is linear or nonlinear. Most studies examine the linear relationship ([Corbet et al.](#corbet,-s.,-larkin,-c.,-lucey,-b.,-2020b.-the-contagion-effects-of-the-covid–19-pandemic:-evidence-from-gold-and-cryptocurrencies.-finance-res.-lett.-35,-101554.), [2020a](#corbet,-s.,-larkin,-c.,-lucey,-b.,-2020b.-the-contagion-effects-of-the-covid–19-pandemic:-evidence-from-gold-and-cryptocurrencies.-finance-res.-lett.-35,-101554.)). We anticipate a nonlinear relationship, and [we](#brenner,-m.,-pasquariello,-p.,-subrahmanyam,-m.,-2009.-on-the-volatility-and-comovement-of-us-financial-markets-around-macroeconomic-news-announcements.-j.-financ.-quant.-anal.-44-\(6\),-1265–1289.) use the Brock, Dechert and Scheinkman (BDS) test of [Broock](#brenner,-m.,-pasquariello,-p.,-subrahmanyam,-m.,-2009.-on-the-volatility-and-comovement-of-us-financial-markets-around-macroeconomic-news-announcements.-j.-financ.-quant.-anal.-44-\(6\),-1265–1289.) [et al.](#brenner,-m.,-pasquariello,-p.,-subrahmanyam,-m.,-2009.-on-the-volatility-and-comovement-of-us-financial-markets-around-macroeconomic-news-announcements.-j.-financ.-quant.-anal.-44-\(6\),-1265–1289.) ([1996](#brenner,-m.,-pasquariello,-p.,-subrahmanyam,-m.,-2009.-on-the-volatility-and-comovement-of-us-financial-markets-around-macroeconomic-news-announcements.-j.-financ.-quant.-anal.-44-\(6\),-1265–1289.)) to examine the nonlinear structure in the return se- ries. The results of the BDS test reveal a nonlinear structure in the cryptocurrency return series. Hence, a nonlinear technique is bet- ter adapted to capture cryptocurrencies’ return and volatility dy- namics. We employ transfer entropy (TE), which measures asym- [metric](#22-\(1\),-79–86.-http://dx.doi.org/10.24425/124266.) information flow and causality in complex systems ([Kwon](#22-\(1\),-79–86.-http://dx.doi.org/10.24425/124266.) [and Oh](#22-\(1\),-79–86.-http://dx.doi.org/10.24425/124266.), [2012](#22-\(1\),-79–86.-http://dx.doi.org/10.24425/124266.); [Marschinski and Kantz](#luss,-r.,-d’aspremont,-a.,-2015.-predicting-abnormal-returns-from-news-using-text-classification.-quant.-finance-15-\(6\),-999–1012.), [2002](#luss,-r.,-d’aspremont,-a.,-2015.-predicting-abnormal-returns-from-news-using-text-classification.-quant.-finance-15-\(6\),-999–1012.)). Though literature explored the information flow in financial markets, TE widens [the](#luss,-r.,-d’aspremont,-a.,-2015.-predicting-abnormal-returns-from-news-using-text-classification.-quant.-finance-15-\(6\),-999–1012.) possibility of detecting nonlinear relationships. [Marschinski](#luss,-r.,-d’aspremont,-a.,-2015.-predicting-abnormal-returns-from-news-using-text-classification.-quant.-finance-15-\(6\),-999–1012.) [and Kantz](#luss,-r.,-d’aspremont,-a.,-2015.-predicting-abnormal-returns-from-news-using-text-classification.-quant.-finance-15-\(6\),-999–1012.) ([2002](#luss,-r.,-d’aspremont,-a.,-2015.-predicting-abnormal-returns-from-news-using-text-classification.-quant.-finance-15-\(6\),-999–1012.)) use TE to measure the relationship between the U.S. Dow Jones Industrial Average and the German DAX Xetra Stock Index. In contrast, [Kwon and Yang](#kwon,-o.,-oh,-g.,-2012.-asymmetric-information-flow-between-market-index-and-individual-stocks-in-several-stock-markets.-europhys.-lett.-97-\(2\),-28007.) ([2008](#kwon,-o.,-oh,-g.,-2012.-asymmetric-information-flow-between-market-index-and-individual-stocks-in-several-stock-markets.-europhys.-lett.-97-\(2\),-28007.)) substantiated that the US stock market impacts major stock market indexes globally by applying TE. [Sensoy et al.](#schreiber,-t.,-2000.-measuring-information-transfer.-phys.-rev.-lett.-85-\(2\),-461–464.-http://dx.doi.org/10.1103/physrevlett.85.461.) ([2014](#schreiber,-t.,-2000.-measuring-information-transfer.-phys.-rev.-lett.-85-\(2\),-461–464.-http://dx.doi.org/10.1103/physrevlett.85.461.)) found a robust nonlinear relationship between exchange rates and stock prices.  
The literature relating the COVID-19 pandemic to financial markets, including cryptocurrencies, has been evolving since the onset of the pandemic. For example, [Corbet et al.](#corbet,-s.,-hou,-y.g.,-hu,-y.,-larkin,-c.,-oxley,-l.,-2020c.-any-port-in-a-storm:-cryptocurrency-safe-havens-during-the-covid–19-pandemic.-econom.-lett.-194,-109377.) ([2020b](#corbet,-s.,-hou,-y.g.,-hu,-y.,-larkin,-c.,-oxley,-l.,-2020c.-any-port-in-a-storm:-cryptocurrency-safe-havens-during-the-covid–19-pandemic.-econom.-lett.-194,-109377.)) show [that](#akhtaruzzaman,-m.,-boubaker,-s.,-lucey,-b.m.,-sensoy,-a.,-2021b.-is-gold-a-hedge-or-a-safe-haven-asset-in-the-covid–19-crisis?-econ.-model.-102,-105588.) the COVID crisis has negatively impacted firms. [Akhtaruzza-](#akhtaruzzaman,-m.,-boubaker,-s.,-lucey,-b.m.,-sensoy,-a.,-2021b.-is-gold-a-hedge-or-a-safe-haven-asset-in-the-covid–19-crisis?-econ.-model.-102,-105588.) [man et al.](#akhtaruzzaman,-m.,-boubaker,-s.,-lucey,-b.m.,-sensoy,-a.,-2021b.-is-gold-a-hedge-or-a-safe-haven-asset-in-the-covid–19-crisis?-econ.-model.-102,-105588.) ([2021a](#akhtaruzzaman,-m.,-boubaker,-s.,-lucey,-b.m.,-sensoy,-a.,-2021b.-is-gold-a-hedge-or-a-safe-haven-asset-in-the-covid–19-crisis?-econ.-model.-102,-105588.)) report that firms across G7 countries and China significantly rose in conditional correlation. The study results support the findings of [Banerjee](#bailey,-w.,-zheng,-l.,-zhou,-y.,-2014.-what-makes-the-vix-tick?.-available-at-ssrn-2143891.) ([2021](#bailey,-w.,-zheng,-l.,-zhou,-y.,-2014.-what-makes-the-vix-tick?.-available-at-ssrn-2143891.)), who report that cross- market linkages cause contagion in futures markets in both de- veloped and emerging countries. Apart from financial contagion during the pandemic, the literature shows the changing dynamics of gold as a safe-haven property ([Akhtaruzzaman et al.](#akhtaruzzaman,-m.,-boubaker,-s.,-chiah,-m.,-zhong,-a.,-2020a.-covid-19-and-oil-price-risk-exposure.-finance-res.-lett.-101882.), [2021b](#akhtaruzzaman,-m.,-boubaker,-s.,-chiah,-m.,-zhong,-a.,-2020a.-covid-19-and-oil-price-risk-exposure.-finance-res.-lett.-101882.)). The pandemic moderates the oil price exposure of industries ([Akhtaruzzaman et al.](#aharon,-d.y.,-2020.-uncertainty,-fear-and-herding-behavior:-evidence-from-size-ranked-portfolios.-j.-behav.-finance-1–18.), [2020a](#aharon,-d.y.,-2020.-uncertainty,-fear-and-herding-behavior:-evidence-from-size-ranked-portfolios.-j.-behav.-finance-1–18.); [Banerjee and Pradhan](#banerjee,-a.k.,-pradhan,-h.k.,-2021a.-intraday-analysis-of-macroeconomic-news-surprises,-and-asymmetries-in-indian-benchmark-bond.-finance-res.-lett.-102135.), [2021b](#banerjee,-a.k.,-pradhan,-h.k.,-2021a.-intraday-analysis-of-macroeconomic-news-surprises,-and-asymmetries-in-indian-benchmark-bond.-finance-res.-lett.-102135.)).

COVID-19 period. Recent studies examine the interaction be- tween cryptocurrency and other asset classes like foreign ex- change, commodities, and stocks ([Akhtaruzzaman et al.](#akhtaruzzaman,-m.,-boubaker,-s.,-umar,-z.,-2021c.-covid–19-media-coverage-and-esg-leader-indices.-finance-res.-lett.-102170.), [2020b](#akhtaruzzaman,-m.,-boubaker,-s.,-umar,-z.,-2021c.-covid–19-media-coverage-and-esg-leader-indices.-finance-res.-lett.-102170.); [Pho et al.](#philippas,-d.,-rjiba,-h.,-guesmi,-k.,-goutte,-s.,-2019.-media-attention-and-bitcoin-prices.-finance-res.-lett.-30,-37–43.), [2021](#philippas,-d.,-rjiba,-h.,-guesmi,-k.,-goutte,-s.,-2019.-media-attention-and-bitcoin-prices.-finance-res.-lett.-30,-37–43.)). [Gajardo et al.](#fu,-l.,-boehe,-d.,-akhtaruzzaman,-m.,-2021.-culture-and-mixed-signals:-does-esg-reduce-risk-everywhere?-in:-academy-of-management-proceedings.-p.-10306.-gajardo,-g.,-kristjanpoller,-w.d.,-minutolo,-m.,-2018.-does-bitcoin-exhibit-the-same-asymmetric-multifractal-cross-correlations-with-crude-oil,-gold-and-djia-as-the-euro,-great-british-pound-and-yen?-chaos-solitons-fractals-109,) ([2018](#fu,-l.,-boehe,-d.,-akhtaruzzaman,-m.,-2021.-culture-and-mixed-signals:-does-esg-reduce-risk-everywhere?-in:-academy-of-management-proceedings.-p.-10306.-gajardo,-g.,-kristjanpoller,-w.d.,-minutolo,-m.,-2018.-does-bitcoin-exhibit-the-same-asymmetric-multifractal-cross-correlations-with-crude-oil,-gold-and-djia-as-the-euro,-great-british-pound-and-yen?-chaos-solitons-fractals-109,)) propose a non-symmetrical association between Bitcoin and equity markets. [Aste](#aslanidis,-n.,-bariviera,-a.f.,-perez-laborda,-a.,-2021.-are-cryptocurrencies-becoming-more-interconnected?-econom.-lett.-199,-109725.) ([2019](#aslanidis,-n.,-bariviera,-a.f.,-perez-laborda,-a.,-2021.-are-cryptocurrencies-becoming-more-interconnected?-econom.-lett.-199,-109725.)) and [Gkillas et al.](#//dx.doi.org/10.3390/e17010438.) ([2018](#//dx.doi.org/10.3390/e17010438.)) report that intra-market correlation among cryptocurrencies exhibits non-normal statistical properties in price fluctuation. Some of the recent literature discusses the [effects](#comincioli,-b.,-1996.-the-stock-market-as-a-leading-indicator:-an-application-of-granger-causality.-univ.-ave.-undergrad.-j.-econ.-1-\(1\),-1.) of COVID-19 on cryptocurrency markets (e.g., see [Conlon](#comincioli,-b.,-1996.-the-stock-market-as-a-leading-indicator:-an-application-of-granger-causality.-univ.-ave.-undergrad.-j.-econ.-1-\(1\),-1.) [et al.](#comincioli,-b.,-1996.-the-stock-market-as-a-leading-indicator:-an-application-of-granger-causality.-univ.-ave.-undergrad.-j.-econ.-1-\(1\),-1.), [2020](#comincioli,-b.,-1996.-the-stock-market-as-a-leading-indicator:-an-application-of-granger-causality.-univ.-ave.-undergrad.-j.-econ.-1-\(1\),-1.); [Lahmiri and Bekiros](#lett.-82-\(6\),-68003.), [2020](#lett.-82-\(6\),-68003.); [Wang et al.](#výrost,-t.,-lyócsa,-š.,-baumöhl,-e.,-2015.-granger-causality-stock-market-net--works:-temporal-proximity-and-preferential-attachment.-physica-a-427,-262–276.), [2019](#výrost,-t.,-lyócsa,-š.,-baumöhl,-e.,-2015.-granger-causality-stock-market-net--works:-temporal-proximity-and-preferential-attachment.-physica-a-427,-262–276.)). Several authors analysed if the COVID-19 pandemic affected the relationship between cryptocurrencies. For example, [Bouri et al.](#bouri,-e.,-gupta,-r.,-lahiani,-a.,-shahbaz,-m.,-2018.-testing-for-asymmetric-nonlin--ear-short-and-long-run-relationships-between-bitcoin,-aggregate-commodity-and-gold-prices.-resour.-policy-57,-224–235.) ([2021b](#bouri,-e.,-gupta,-r.,-lahiani,-a.,-shahbaz,-m.,-2018.-testing-for-asymmetric-nonlin--ear-short-and-long-run-relationships-between-bitcoin,-aggregate-commodity-and-gold-prices.-resour.-policy-57,-224–235.)) applied quantile-based connectedness measures. They revealed that the connectedness measures in the left and right tails are much higher than those in the mean and median of the conditional distribution, indicating that return shocks propagate more intensely during extreme events relative to calm periods. [Aslanidis et al.](#anamika,-a.,-subramaniam,-s.,-2022.-do-news-headlines-matter-in-the-cryptocurrency-market?-appl.-econ.-1–17.) ([2021](#anamika,-a.,-subramaniam,-s.,-2022.-do-news-headlines-matter-in-the-cryptocurrency-market?-appl.-econ.-1–17.)) aimed to answer whether cryptocurrencies are becoming more integrated between August 2015 and July 2020\. They find a substantial increase in market linkages for both returns and volatilities, indicating a tighter relationship among cryptocurrencies in the COVID-19 period. [Demiralay and Golitsis](#econ.-58-\(2–3\),-275–326.) ([2021](#econ.-58-\(2–3\),-275–326.)) investigated the time-varying comovements employing a dynamic equicorrelation GARCH (DECO-GARCH) model in crypto markets. The study results show that the comovements across cryptos increased substantially in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic. However, most studies ignore the possibility of the relationship’s nonlinear or asymmetric nature ([Baur and Dimpfl](#barnett,-l.,-barrett,-a.b.,-seth,-a.k.,-2009.-granger-causality-and-transfer-entropy-are-equivalent-for-gaussian-variables.-phys.-rev.-lett.-103-\(23\),-http://dx.doi.-org/10.1103/physrevlett.103.238701.), [2018](#barnett,-l.,-barrett,-a.b.,-seth,-a.k.,-2009.-granger-causality-and-transfer-entropy-are-equivalent-for-gaussian-variables.-phys.-rev.-lett.-103-\(23\),-http://dx.doi.-org/10.1103/physrevlett.103.238701.)). Changes in news content related to the COVID-19 crisis may have a differential impact on the prices of cryptocurrencies. [Akyildirim et al.](#akhtaruzzaman,-m.,-sensoy,-a.,-corbet,-s.,-2020b.-the-influence-of-bitcoin-on-portfolio-diversification-and-design.-finance-res.-lett.-37,-101344.) ([2021](#akhtaruzzaman,-m.,-sensoy,-a.,-corbet,-s.,-2020b.-the-influence-of-bitcoin-on-portfolio-diversification-and-design.-finance-res.-lett.-37,-101344.)) studied the dynamic network con- nectedness between 13 leading cryptos by market capitalisation and MarketPsych indices. The results supported the dominance of cryptocurrencies with higher market capitalisation. However, Bitcoin was losing its dominance to altcoins in return spillovers while still dominating in sentiment spillovers. Moreover, past studies emphasised that Bitcoin is against other major cryptocur- rencies that tend to have a significant presence in the market ([Corbet et al.](#corbet,-s.,-larkin,-c.,-lucey,-b.,-2020b.-the-contagion-effects-of-the-covid–19-pandemic:-evidence-from-gold-and-cryptocurrencies.-finance-res.-lett.-35,-101554.), [2020a](#corbet,-s.,-larkin,-c.,-lucey,-b.,-2020b.-the-contagion-effects-of-the-covid–19-pandemic:-evidence-from-gold-and-cryptocurrencies.-finance-res.-lett.-35,-101554.); [Oad Rajput et al.](#nelson,-d.b.,-1991.-conditional-heteroskedasticity-in-asset-returns:-a-new-approach.-econometrica-59-\(2\),-347–370.), [2020](#nelson,-d.b.,-1991.-conditional-heteroskedasticity-in-asset-returns:-a-new-approach.-econometrica-59-\(2\),-347–370.)). However, there is a void in the literature studying the impact of different COVID-19 news sentiments on major cryptos. We address this void in this study by examining the nexus between the top 30 cryptocurren- cies (constituting approximately 79% of total market capitalisa- tion) and COVID-19 news sentiment obtained from the Ravenpack database. In contrast, some studies have found an association between other sources of news sentiment like Google Trend or MarketPsych indices and volatility ([Akhtaruzzaman et al.](#akhtaruzzaman,-m.,-boubaker,-s.,-sensoy,-a.,-2021a.-financial-contagion-during-covid–19-crisis.-finance-res.-lett.-38,-101604.), [2021c](#akhtaruzzaman,-m.,-boubaker,-s.,-sensoy,-a.,-2021a.-financial-contagion-during-covid–19-crisis.-finance-res.-lett.-38,-101604.); [Akyildirim et al.](#akhtaruzzaman,-m.,-sensoy,-a.,-corbet,-s.,-2020b.-the-influence-of-bitcoin-on-portfolio-diversification-and-design.-finance-res.-lett.-37,-101344.), [2021](#akhtaruzzaman,-m.,-sensoy,-a.,-corbet,-s.,-2020b.-the-influence-of-bitcoin-on-portfolio-diversification-and-design.-finance-res.-lett.-37,-101344.); [Blitz et al.](#behrendt,-s.,-dimpfl,-t.,-peter,-f.j.,-zimmermann,-d.j.,-2019.-r-transfer-entropy—-quantifying-information-flow-between-different-time-series-using-effective-transfer-entropy.-softwarex-10,-100265.), [2020](#behrendt,-s.,-dimpfl,-t.,-peter,-f.j.,-zimmermann,-d.j.,-2019.-r-transfer-entropy—-quantifying-information-flow-between-different-time-series-using-effective-transfer-entropy.-softwarex-10,-100265.); [Philippas et al.](#osei,-p.m.,-adam,-a.m.,-2020.-quantifying-the-information-flow-between-ghana-stock-market-index-and-its-constituents-using-transfer-entropy.-math.-probl.-eng..), [2019](#osei,-p.m.,-adam,-a.m.,-2020.-quantifying-the-information-flow-between-ghana-stock-market-index-and-its-constituents-using-transfer-entropy.-math.-probl.-eng..);  
[Shi and Ho](#j.-27-\(3\),-379–423.), [2021](#j.-27-\(3\),-379–423.); [Smales](#sifat,-i.,-2021.-on-cryptocurrencies-as-an-independent-asset-class:-long-horizon-and-covid–19-pandemic-era-decoupling-from-global-sentiments.-finance-res.-lett.-102013.), [2014](#sifat,-i.,-2021.-on-cryptocurrencies-as-an-independent-asset-class:-long-horizon-and-covid–19-pandemic-era-decoupling-from-global-sentiments.-finance-res.-lett.-102013.); [Lin](#lahmiri,-s.,-bekiros,-s.,-2020.-the-impact-of-covid–19-pandemic-upon-stability-and-sequential-irregularity-of-equity-and-cryptocurrency-markets.-chaos-solitons-fractals-138,-109936.), [2021](#lahmiri,-s.,-bekiros,-s.,-2020.-the-impact-of-covid–19-pandemic-upon-stability-and-sequential-irregularity-of-equity-and-cryptocurrency-markets.-chaos-solitons-fractals-138,-109936.)).[3](#shi-and-ho,-2021;-smales,-2014;-lin,-2021\).3)  
The study is the first to analyse the differential impact of dif- ferent categories of COVID–19 news sentiment on the behaviour of cryptocurrency returns. We investigate the reaction of the top 30 cryptocurrencies to COVID-19 news over the sample period from January 1, 2020 to April 15, 2021\. The results indicate a significant positive nonlinear relationship between cryptocurren- cies’ return and news sentiment related to COVID-19. The re- sults reflect that cryptocurrencies witnessed a bullish run during the study period, and some of these reacted more to COVID– 19 developments. In particular, the media portrayal of COVID–19 conditions influences most cryptocurrency returns, which is more pronounced with Bitcoin Cash, DASH, Tether, and DAI.  
Cryptocurrencies react vigorously to media exaggeration, where the recent Dogecoin fiasco represents a glaring example of market overreaction and herd behaviour ([Hobbs](#heston,-s.l.,-sinha,-n.r.,-2017.-news-vs.-sentiment:-predicting-stock-returns-from-news-stories.-financ.-anal.-j.-73-\(3\),-67–83.), [2021](#heston,-s.l.,-sinha,-n.r.,-2017.-news-vs.-sentiment:-predicting-stock-returns-from-news-stories.-financ.-anal.-j.-73-\(3\),-67–83.)). In  
Moreover, [Goodell and Goutte](#glosten,-l.r.,-jagannathan,-r.,-runkle,-d.e.,-1993.-on-the-relation-between-the-expected-value-and-the-volatility-of-the-nominal-excess-return-on-stocks.-j.-finance-48-\(5\),-1779–1801.) ([2021](#glosten,-l.r.,-jagannathan,-r.,-runkle,-d.e.,-1993.-on-the-relation-between-the-expected-value-and-the-volatility-of-the-nominal-excess-return-on-stocks.-j.-finance-48-\(5\),-1779–1801.)) emphasise that cryp-

comparison, fake and sentiment news have the most negligible impact on cryptocurrencies compared to other news sentiment indices. Globally, the news sentiment related to the COVID-19 influence almost all the cryptocurrency returns, contradicting the finding of [Akyildirim et al.](#akhtaruzzaman,-m.,-sensoy,-a.,-corbet,-s.,-2020b.-the-influence-of-bitcoin-on-portfolio-diversification-and-design.-finance-res.-lett.-37,-101344.) ([2021](#akhtaruzzaman,-m.,-sensoy,-a.,-corbet,-s.,-2020b.-the-influence-of-bitcoin-on-portfolio-diversification-and-design.-finance-res.-lett.-37,-101344.)). Thus, these results hold valuable insights for market participants. Moreover, uncertainty became relatively high in Ripple and saw a sudden price spurt during the pandemic ([Bouri et al.](#boudoukh,-j.,-feldman,-r.,-kogan,-s.,-richardson,-m.,-2013.-which-news-moves-stock-prices?-a-textual-analysis-\(no.-w18725\).-national-bureau-of-economic-research.), [2021a](#boudoukh,-j.,-feldman,-r.,-kogan,-s.,-richardson,-m.,-2013.-which-news-moves-stock-prices?-a-textual-analysis-\(no.-w18725\).-national-bureau-of-economic-research.)). The recent bullish run seen in cryptocurrency prices does not reflect fundamental value. These episodes suggest the presence of considerable specula- tion and inefficiency in these markets ([Dowd](#dowd,-k.,-2014.-new-private-monies:-a-bit-part-player?.-institute-of-economic-affairs-monographs,-hobart-paper,-174.), [2014](#dowd,-k.,-2014.-new-private-monies:-a-bit-part-player?.-institute-of-economic-affairs-monographs,-hobart-paper,-174.)), potentially leading to bubbles ([Dale et al.](#cutler,-d.m.,-poterba,-j.m.,-summers,-l.h.,-1989.-what-moves-stock-prices?-j.-portf.-manage.-15-\(3\),-4–12.), [2005](#cutler,-d.m.,-poterba,-j.m.,-summers,-l.h.,-1989.-what-moves-stock-prices?-j.-portf.-manage.-15-\(3\),-4–12.)). These results also support concerns over cryptocurrencies’ long-term viability for portfolio diversification, as excessive volatility and lower liquidity diminish the diversification benefits. Finally, these results give investors, policymakers, and regulators practical insights. This paper pro- ceeds as follows. Section [2](#the-source-of-news-sentiment-data-on-the-covid-19-panic,) describes the data and descriptive statistics, Section [3](#analysis-of-causality-holds-great-importance-in-studying-fi--nancial-market-behaviour,-and-linear-granger-causality-is-most-commonly-used-to-understand-causal-behaviour.-however,-at--tempts-to-understand-behaviour-and-directional-causality-have-motivated-researchers-to-search-for-more-efficient-and-global-approaches-\(see,-for-example,-abdennadher-and-hellara,-2018;-agbloyor-et-al.,-2013;-comincioli,-1996;-stavroglou-et-al.,-2019\).-however,-the-credit-for-testing-causality-goes-to-granger-\(1969\);-the-granger-causality-test-\(gc\)-is-one-of-the-most-popularly-used-in-the-financial-literature-to-evaluate-the-bidirectional-relation--ship-between-variables.-gc-assesses-how-past-values-of-a-given-variable-impact-another-variable-in-a-vector-autoregressive-\(var\)-framework,-including-past-and-present-values-of-both-variables.) discusses the methodology, and the empirical results are part of Section [4](#to-quantify-the-information-flow-between-news-sentiment-in--dices-related-to-the-covid–19-and-the-cryptocurrency-returns,-we-applied-te.-the-results-show-that-panic,-media-hype,-fake-news,-infodemic,-sentiment-and-the-media-coverage-index-of-covid-). Finally, Section [5](#this-study-explores-the-impact-of-six-covid-19-news-senti--ment-indices-on-the-market-returns-of-the-top-30-cryptocurrencies-by-market-capitalisation.-we-check-how-news-about-the-intensity-of-the-pandemic-affects-the-returns-of-these-cryptocurrencies-using-the-nonlinear-technique-of-te.-results-reveal-that-the-as--sociation-between-covid-19-news-sentiment-and-cryptocurrency-returns-is-nonlinear,-thus-supporting-bouri-et-al.-\(2018\)-findings.) sets forth our conclusions.

The augmented Dickey–Fuller test (ADF) and Philip–Perron (PP) test demonstrate that cryptocurrency return series are sta- tionary (see [Table](#table-2-1) [2](#table-2-1)). The media coverage index rose sharply during the beginning of the pandemic and peaked in March, coinciding with the period when the World Health Organization (WHO) declared COVID-19 a pandemic.[6](#significant-level,5-consistent-with-the-regular-stylised-fact-of-fat-tails.-the-augmented-dickey–fuller-test-\(adf\)-and-philip–perron-\(pp\)-test-demonstrate-that-cryptocurrency-return-series-are-sta--tionary-\(see-table-2\).-the-media-coverage-index-rose-sharply-during-the-beginning-of-the-pandemic-and-peaked-in-march,-coinciding-with-the-period-when-the-world-health-organization-\(who\)-declared-covid-19-a-pandemic.6-the-highest-media-cov--erage-index,-in-march-2020,-reflects-that-global-financial-markets-witnessed-sharp-declines-\(akhtaruzzaman-et-al.,-2021a\).-simi--larly,-the-panic,-media-hype,-and-infodemic-indices-peaked-in-march-2020.7-interestingly,-many-cryptocurrencies-experienced-jumps-in-volatility-in-march-2020-and-february–march-2021.-the-higher-volatility-in-march-2020-is-due-to-the-onset-of-the-pandemic-\(corbet-et-al.,-2021\).-the-latter-episode-of-volatility-in-2021-reflects-a-surge,-partly-attributed-to-statements-made-by-elon-musk-\(hobbs,-2021\).-moreover,-the-volatility-pattern-reflects-that-the-markets-react-immediately-to-news-related-to-covid-19) The highest media cov- erage index, in March 2020, reflects that global financial markets witnessed sharp declines ([Akhtaruzzaman et al.](#akhtaruzzaman,-m.,-boubaker,-s.,-lucey,-b.m.,-sensoy,-a.,-2021b.-is-gold-a-hedge-or-a-safe-haven-asset-in-the-covid–19-crisis?-econ.-model.-102,-105588.), [2021a](#akhtaruzzaman,-m.,-boubaker,-s.,-lucey,-b.m.,-sensoy,-a.,-2021b.-is-gold-a-hedge-or-a-safe-haven-asset-in-the-covid–19-crisis?-econ.-model.-102,-105588.)). Simi- larly, the panic, media hype, and infodemic indices peaked in March 2020\.[7](#significant-level,5-consistent-with-the-regular-stylised-fact-of-fat-tails.-the-augmented-dickey–fuller-test-\(adf\)-and-philip–perron-\(pp\)-test-demonstrate-that-cryptocurrency-return-series-are-sta--tionary-\(see-table-2\).-the-media-coverage-index-rose-sharply-during-the-beginning-of-the-pandemic-and-peaked-in-march,-coinciding-with-the-period-when-the-world-health-organization-\(who\)-declared-covid-19-a-pandemic.6-the-highest-media-cov--erage-index,-in-march-2020,-reflects-that-global-financial-markets-witnessed-sharp-declines-\(akhtaruzzaman-et-al.,-2021a\).-simi--larly,-the-panic,-media-hype,-and-infodemic-indices-peaked-in-march-2020.7-interestingly,-many-cryptocurrencies-experienced-jumps-in-volatility-in-march-2020-and-february–march-2021.-the-higher-volatility-in-march-2020-is-due-to-the-onset-of-the-pandemic-\(corbet-et-al.,-2021\).-the-latter-episode-of-volatility-in-2021-reflects-a-surge,-partly-attributed-to-statements-made-by-elon-musk-\(hobbs,-2021\).-moreover,-the-volatility-pattern-reflects-that-the-markets-react-immediately-to-news-related-to-covid-19) Interestingly, many cryptocurrencies experienced jumps in volatility in March 2020 and February–March 2021\. The higher volatility in March 2020 is due to the onset of the pandemic ([Corbet et al.](#connelly,-b.l.,-certo,-s.t.,-ireland,-r.d.,-reutzel,-c.r.,-2011.-signaling-theory:-a-review-and-assessment.-j.-manage.-37-\(1\),-39–67.), [2021](#connelly,-b.l.,-certo,-s.t.,-ireland,-r.d.,-reutzel,-c.r.,-2011.-signaling-theory:-a-review-and-assessment.-j.-manage.-37-\(1\),-39–67.)). The latter episode of volatility in 2021 reflects a surge, partly attributed to statements made by Elon Musk ([Hobbs](#heston,-s.l.,-sinha,-n.r.,-2017.-news-vs.-sentiment:-predicting-stock-returns-from-news-stories.-financ.-anal.-j.-73-\(3\),-67–83.), [2021](#heston,-s.l.,-sinha,-n.r.,-2017.-news-vs.-sentiment:-predicting-stock-returns-from-news-stories.-financ.-anal.-j.-73-\(3\),-67–83.)). Moreover, the volatility pattern reflects that the markets react immediately to news related to COVID-19

3. **Methodology**

Analysis of causality holds great importance in studying fi- nancial market behaviour, and linear Granger causality is most commonly used to understand causal behaviour. However, at- tempts to understand behaviour and directional causality have motivated researchers to search for more efficient and global approaches (see, for example, [Abdennadher and Hellara](#abdennadher,-e.,-hellara,-s.,-2018.-causality-and-contagion-in-emerging-stock-markets.-borsa-istanb.-rev.-18-\(4\),-300–311.), [2018](#abdennadher,-e.,-hellara,-s.,-2018.-causality-and-contagion-in-emerging-stock-markets.-borsa-istanb.-rev.-18-\(4\),-300–311.); [Agbloyor et al.](#abdennadher,-e.,-hellara,-s.,-2018.-causality-and-contagion-in-emerging-stock-markets.-borsa-istanb.-rev.-18-\(4\),-300–311.), [2013](#abdennadher,-e.,-hellara,-s.,-2018.-causality-and-contagion-in-emerging-stock-markets.-borsa-istanb.-rev.-18-\(4\),-300–311.); [Comincioli](#ciaian,-p.,-rajcaniova,-m.,-kancs,-d.a.,-2016.-the-economics-of-bitcoin-price-formation.-appl.-econ.-48-\(19\),-1799–1815.), [1996](#ciaian,-p.,-rajcaniova,-m.,-kancs,-d.a.,-2016.-the-economics-of-bitcoin-price-formation.-appl.-econ.-48-\(19\),-1799–1815.); [Stavroglou et al.](#49,-275–286.), [2019](#49,-275–286.)). However, the credit for testing causality goes to [Granger](#goodell,-j.w.,-goutte,-s.,-2021.-co-movement-of-covid–19-and-bitcoin:-evidence-from-wavelet-coherence-analysis.-finance-res.-lett.-38,-101625.) ([1969](#goodell,-j.w.,-goutte,-s.,-2021.-co-movement-of-covid–19-and-bitcoin:-evidence-from-wavelet-coherence-analysis.-finance-res.-lett.-38,-101625.)); the Granger causality test (GC) is one of the most popularly used in the financial literature to evaluate the bidirectional relation- ship between variables. GC assesses how past values of a given variable impact another variable in a vector autoregressive (VAR) framework, including past and present values of both variables.

Formally, a given variable *Y* Granger causes *X*, with lags *k* and

5. Figures A1 and A2 in the appendix present the price and return series, respectively, of the 30 cryptocurrencies.  
6. Figure A3 in the appendix presents sentiment news indices by Ravenpack.

7. Figure A4 in the appendix presents the conditional volatility of cryptocur- rency returns. Conditional volatility is estimated using a GARCH (1,1) model with a constant as the only regressor. We estimate the conditional volatility of cryptocurrency return using other GARCH models: GJR-GARCH ([Glosten et al.](#gkillas,-k.,-bekiros,-s.,-siriopoulos,-c.,-2018.-extreme-correlation-in-cryptocur--rency-markets.-available-at-ssrn-3180934.), [1993](#gkillas,-k.,-bekiros,-s.,-siriopoulos,-c.,-2018.-extreme-correlation-in-cryptocur--rency-markets.-available-at-ssrn-3180934.)); EGARCH ([Nelson](#naeem,-m.a.,-mbarki,-i.,-suleman,-m.t.,-vo,-x.v.,-shahzad,-s.j.h.,-2020.-does-twitter-happiness-sentiment-predict-cryptocurrency?-int.-rev.-financ..), [1991](#naeem,-m.a.,-mbarki,-i.,-suleman,-m.t.,-vo,-x.v.,-shahzad,-s.j.h.,-2020.-does-twitter-happiness-sentiment-predict-cryptocurrency?-int.-rev.-financ..)); IGARCH ([Engle and Bollerslev](#dowd,-k.,-2014.-new-private-monies:-a-bit-part-player?.-institute-of-economic-affairs-monographs,-hobart-paper,-174.), [1986](#dowd,-k.,-2014.-new-private-monies:-a-bit-part-player?.-institute-of-economic-affairs-monographs,-hobart-paper,-174.)); APARCH ([Ding et al.](#dimpfl,-t.,-peter,-f.j.,-2014.-the-impact-of-the-financial-crisis-on-transatlantic-information-flows:-an-intraday-analysis.-j.-int.-financ.-mark.-inst.-money-31-\(1\),-1–13.-http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.intfin.2014.03.004.), [1993](#dimpfl,-t.,-peter,-f.j.,-2014.-the-impact-of-the-financial-crisis-on-transatlantic-information-flows:-an-intraday-analysis.-j.-int.-financ.-mark.-inst.-money-31-\(1\),-1–13.-http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.intfin.2014.03.004.)) for our robustness check. We find similar conditional volatility of cryptocurrency return using these alternative GARCH models.

Granger causality is one of the best-known causality measures significantly used in major causality studies in the financial mar- ket. However, as it is a second-order statisitics, focusing on correlation-centred measure which has a severe limitation. It is limited to analysing the linear impact between variables, limiting its relevance to linear systems ([Gencaga et al.](#garcía,-c.j.,-herrero,-b.,-ibáñez,-a.m.,-2014.-information-and-investor-behavior-surrounding-earnings-announcements.-j.-behav.-finance-15-\(2\),-133–143.), [2015](#garcía,-c.j.,-herrero,-b.,-ibáñez,-a.m.,-2014.-information-and-investor-behavior-surrounding-earnings-announcements.-j.-behav.-finance-15-\(2\),-133–143.)). As such, it may lead to a loss of information when the relationships between variables have nonlinear structures. Therefore, it is critical to use more global measures to capture both the linear and the nonlinear relationship between variables or between markets.
